chapter: Los Angeles nightlife: Sheffield, Hamp and the Cotton Club
title: The raid where Sheffield said Every tub
summary: Joe tells of a house-rent party where Sheffield joked Every tub, and mentions the other detectives Black Benny and Green.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Any musician that lived here in Los Angeles that had two tough cops... Sheffield was a Black policeman, and they had a White policeman named Sweetman -- which was a tough character, too. They caught you in one of them joints, they'd put you in jail. But what Sheffield would do, now... They claimed Sheffield was bad. He was bad on people that he didn't know. But he never hardly bothered musicians unless he caught you drunk, and you got a little smart or belligerent with him. He usually would let you go. I remember well, one time we was playing in this joint, and some guy said, "Run, Sheffield's coming. Frank was playing his guitar and I'm playing the..."
I think Hampton was playing in there, too -- playing drums. And I can't think of the other

musicians in there. Maybe Blakeney was there. I can't remember. But when he said, "Sheffield"... I didn't know Sheffield at the time. I knew his reputation. But Frank knew him. And I says, "Lord, I'm gone." Frank said, "No. Come back here. You just stay here. Sheffield ain't gonna bother you." Obviously, he knew these people, and maybe he was getting his little...
His pet word when he was going to raid a place, usually when he said "Every tub..."

Well, when you see Blake, you ask him about it. When Sheffield said, "Every tub," you'd better make yourself a new door or window or something' to get out of that place, or you're goin' downtown in a patrol wagon.
He was going to arrest everybody.

No sooner than he says, "Every tub, a lot of guys they was hopping out of windows." But me and Frank... Because Frank had me by the arm anyway; I couldn't get away. Frank says, "Sheffield ain't gonna bother you." Then he started laughing. He says, "Forget it fellas; I didn't mean that." He says, "I shouldn't have said 'Every tub.'" [LAUGHS]
So you respected him a lot, then, around here, I guess.

Well, if you knew his reputation, you'd respect him, too. So he came in there, and he just walked around and talked to Frank, and if I remember correctly, I shoot hands with him and his partner. And he said, "Okay, just carry on," then he went in the kitchen and was talking to the musician who was having this party, a bass player named Brock. It was a house... They called them house rent parties then. Old Brock used to fix chitlins and ribs and stuff like that.
And he was a musician, too?

His last name was Brock. I can't think of his first name. Anyway, Sheffield stayed in there and had a drink maybe, or whatever, and just left, and didn't bother us. But they had two other detectives. One was named Black Benny and one was named Green. They was kind of rough, too. But nobody had a reputation like Sheffield. But Benny and Green would wheel and deal. They were strictly on the take.
